problem:
Boy Zhenya lives in a building with a total of 100 floors. The elevator takes 1 second to travel between adjacent floors. Unfortunately, only two buttons in the elevator work: “+13 floors” and “-7 floors”. The buttons are pressed instantly.

How many seconds will it take Zhenya to get home from the 1st floor to the 24th floor? (The elevator can only travel to existing floors)

answer_text:
Let \(x\) be the number of times Zhenya presses \(+13\), and let \(y\) be the number of times he presses \(-7\).

He starts on floor 1 and must end on floor 24, so the net change is

\[
24-1=23.
\]

Thus

\[
13x-7y=23.
\]

We need nonnegative integers \(x,y\). Reduce modulo 7:

\[
13x \equiv 23 \pmod 7
\]

\[
6x \equiv 2 \pmod 7.
\]

Since \(6\cdot 6 \equiv 1 \pmod 7\), we get

\[
x \equiv 12 \equiv 5 \pmod 7.
\]

The smallest nonnegative value is \(x=5\). Then

\[
13(5)-7y=23
\]

\[
65-7y=23
\]

\[
7y=42
\]

\[
y=6.
\]

So the minimum number of moves is 5 presses of \(+13\) and 6 presses of \(-7\).

The time is

\[
5\cdot 13 + 6\cdot 7 = 65+42=107
\]

seconds.

One valid route is:

\[
1 \to 14 \to 27 \to 40 \to 53 \to 66 \to 59 \to 52 \to 45 \to 38 \to 31 \to 24,
\]

and all floors are within the 100-floor building.

Therefore, the minimum time is

\[
\boxed{107}
\]
